header.deal: Membership studio business, US and Canada
header.scope: Won: membership online billing only; studio front desks still on Global Payments, phase two undated and dependent on a partner integration.
header.tag_why: The contract sat with the controller until Tobi showed which of their own failed renewals were recoverable, and it was signed four days later. The deciding question was what recovery is worth in their numbers; Global's counter of a terminal bundle on a longer contract, plus Greg's questions about termination fees, was the main pull the other way.

evidence.excerpt: They report member churn to the board every quarter, it had ticked up two quarters running
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: somebody finally split it into people who cancelled and people whose card just failed
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: members who never meant to leave
evidence.label: quote

evidence.excerpt: I want to say a third of the churn? Don't quote me.
evidence.label: opinion

trigger.insight: The evaluation did not start as a payments project. It started as a churn number the board was watching, and payments only came in once someone split churn by cause. The buyer framed the problem as losing members, not as declines or authorization rates. The size of the failed-card share is unverified: the rep's 'a third' is hedged.
trigger.messaging: For membership businesses, lead M10 with churn: 'members who never meant to leave' are revenue you can recover. Drop generic acceptance-uplift language (M4).

evidence.excerpt: Maya. She ran the evaluation, she was in every meeting, she's the one who told me where we stood.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: His signature's on it.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: The paper had gone to Greg and it sat with him for two weeks. Nothing.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: Maya chose us. Greg decided whether anybody got chosen.
evidence.label: opinion

decider.insight: The rep first named the decider based on Maya's own account. The controller, who held and signed the paper, came out only when the interviewer pushed back. Maya chose the vendor. Greg decided whether any switch happened at all, and he stayed silent until he saw his own data.
decider.messaging: Package the customer-data recovery analysis as a finance-ready artifact for the controller, separate from the champion's evaluation story.

evidence.excerpt: they came back with a rate review and a new terminal bundle for the front desks, on a longer contract
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: I didn't see any of it. That's her telling me.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: what readers do you have, do they work inside our studio software, what's the contract term, what does it cost to get out
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: Greg asked about termination fees twice.
evidence.label: fact

competitor.insight: According to Maya, the incumbent responded with hardware and a longer contract rather than an answer on failed payments. That pulled the customer's questions toward the front desk, where we were weakest. The tactic worked enough to keep the studios with Global for now. The transcript does not say whether Greg's exit-cost questions were about leaving Global or leaving us, or whether the terminal bundle was accepted. The rep's view that Global was 'rattled' is his own read.
competitor.messaging: Expect the incumbent to counter with a front-desk terminal bundle on a longer term, and prepare a response on contract term and exit cost before the controller raises it.

evidence.excerpt: Their file, not our average.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: Greg hadn't said a word in two meetings, and he asked for the spreadsheet.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: I opened with the global slide. They have studios in the US and a handful in Canada.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: when I said 'unified commerce,' Maya goes, 'is that the readers?'
evidence.label: quote

message.insight: Recovery (M10) landed only when it was proven on their own failed renewals. An average-based claim like M6 or M4 would not have moved the silent controller. The global opener (M1) drew silence from a business with studios in the US and a handful in Canada. 'Unified commerce' (M3) meant nothing to the buyer beyond hardware, and that hardware is exactly what we could not show working in their software.
message.messaging: Replace the M1 opener for domestic membership businesses with a recoverable-failed-renewals analysis built from the prospect's own export, and stop using 'unified commerce' as a label.

evidence.excerpt: When Greg asked for the spreadsheet.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: Before that I honestly thought we were there to keep the incumbent honest.
evidence.label: opinion

evidence.excerpt: Then we did the data session, and four days later it was signed.
evidence.label: fact

decided.insight: The turning point was the data session. Before it, the contract had stalled with the controller for two weeks and the rep believed we were a stalking horse. After it, the deal signed within four days. Champion enthusiasm did not move the deal; numbers the controller could take away did.
decided.messaging: Make a 'your failed renewals, scored' session a standard step before paper reaches finance, not a rescue move once the contract stalls.

evidence.excerpt: They asked to see our reader working inside their studio management software.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: We couldn't show that live. It runs through a partner integration, and the partner did a call the week after.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: the studio managers will revolt.
evidence.label: quote

evidence.excerpt: Not yet. It depends on the partner piece.
evidence.label: fact

gaps.insight: The front-desk gap did not lose the deal, but it cut the deal in half. Only memberships and online billing moved. The studios stayed with Global with no date, waiting on a partner integration the customer has only seen in the partner's demo, not in their own setup. M3's 'one platform' claim overpromises when the in-store piece depends on a partner and the customer fears a two-screen front desk.
gaps.messaging: Until we can demo the reader live inside common studio software, position in-store as a partner-delivered phase two rather than as one platform today.

evidence.excerpt: members who never meant to leave
evidence.label: quote

evidence.excerpt: when I said 'unified commerce,' Maya goes, 'is that the readers?'
evidence.label: quote

evidence.excerpt: the studio managers will revolt.
evidence.label: quote

language.insight: The question was deferred to Slack and never answered. The phrases cited here came up in other answers.

gaps.question: What exact words did they use for their problem?
gaps.follow_up: Ask the rep on Slack, as agreed, for Maya's and Greg's exact phrases about failed payments, churn and the front desk.

gaps.question: What was the deal size (ACV)?
gaps.follow_up: Ask the rep for the signed annual contract value of the memberships/online billing phase.

gaps.question: How big was the failed-card share of churn?
gaps.follow_up: Ask the rep to confirm the figure with Maya or from the board deck she presented.

gaps.question: Who made the final call, and how do you know?
gaps.follow_up: Ask the rep what Greg needed to see before signing and whether he has a role in approving phase two.

gaps.question: Did the customer accept Global's terminal bundle and longer contract for the front desks, and were Greg's termination-fee questions about Global or about us?
gaps.follow_up: Ask the rep to find out from Maya what term Global now holds at the front desk and what exiting it would cost.

gaps.question: When will the partner integration be ready for phase two?
gaps.follow_up: Ask the solutions engineer (Tobi) or the partner for a date and whether a live demo can run in the customer's own setup.

close.rep_takeaway: Don't take the champion's word on who decides; follow the paper. Here the contract stalled with the controller, and the thing that moved it was the customer's own failed-renewal file, not our global slide or 'unified commerce'. Bring that analysis to finance early, and treat the undated front-desk phase as open ground the incumbent is still holding.
